`161befa9ca00e1a8dfb8bf97ff3685415ad4d55821ea0a4fcfa6d15fc5762708`.

Device smoke passed on an Android 15 x86_64 emulator. The 16-row fixture inbox
rendered, a conversation opened, Mark done worked, and the archived conversation
remained absent after process restart. Gmail controls and Files and links were
absent. A locally saved draft reopened with its exact subject and body, and the
editor remained intact after backgrounding Email OS, opening Android Settings,
and resuming Email OS. Screenshots are [reader before archive](<validation/android-smoke/reader-before-insets.png>),
[draft saved before restart](<validation/android-smoke/draft-saved-before-restart.png>),
and [draft recovered after restart](<validation/android-smoke/draft-recovered-after-restart.png>).

The first Android launch failed at profile-lock acquisition because
`File::try_lock` returned a storage error on Android 15. Android now uses
nonblocking `flock`; desktop still uses `File::try_lock`. The device check also
found status-bar overlap and a visible Files and links control. The current APK
includes safe-area insets, `adjustResize`, and the Android-only control gate; the
focused Android-vs-browser UI test passed. The keyboard stayed hidden during
draft entry, so actual IME layout was not verified. See the
[development smoke steps](development.md#android-fixture-apk).

On 2026-11-14, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run check:all` passed before the
Android lock correction: core tests, generated IPC contract, formatting and
core clippy, all 1,454 frontend tests, frontend typecheck, native clippy, 14
native bridge tests, and production web build. After the lock correction,
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run test:core` passed with 216 unit tests and all core
integration suites, and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run lint:core` passed. The
focused Android control visibility test and the final APK build also passed.

# Current architecture

**Scope:** This is an inventory of architecture that exists in the source tree. It describes code paths and ownership. For feature availability and validation results, see [current status](current-status.md). For the selected first-build scope, see [ADR 0001](adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md). [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) is a historical proposal; its design recommendations are not evidence of implementation.

## Runtime and boundaries

The app has a Vue/TypeScript frontend, a Tauri 2 shell, and the Rust `mail-core` crate. The Rust crate owns persistence and provider operations. The frontend talks through a `MailClient` interface. In native mode, `createTauriMailClient` maps that interface to named Tauri commands. In browser mode, `browser-fake.ts` supplies a synthetic in-memory client. The shared interface and generated wire types are in [client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/client.ts), [tauri-client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/tauri-client.ts), [browser-fake.ts](../src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts), and [generated.ts](../src/lib/ipc/generated.ts). Rust DTOs are the source for generated TypeScript; `crates/mail-core/src/bin/generate-types.rs` generates the file.

The shared Tauri entry point in [lib.rs](../src-tauri/src/lib.rs) holds the module list and the command handler list. [setup.rs](../src-tauri/src/setup.rs) selects fixture or Gmail mode on desktop, opens the corresponding Rust core (fixture mode is the Gmail core on the built-in synthetic provider, ADR 0002) and handles window and run events; [state.rs](../src-tauri/src/state.rs) holds the single `GmailCore`, the draft service, the attachment transfer registry and the close gate; the commands under [commands/](../src-tauri/src/commands) translate IPC to core calls and emit mailbox/draft/close events. Mail rules live in `mail-core`, not the shell. Desktop [main.rs](../src-tauri/src/main.rs) is a thin launcher. Android forces fixture mode and does not run the desktop close/exit gate. A pre-existing legacy fixture database is retired once by [fixture_transition.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/fixture_transition.rs), behind a startup screen (`StartupRoot.vue`, two IPC commands). Android's generated Gradle project is under `src-tauri/gen/android`; setup and build steps are in [development guide](development.md). The webview does not access SQLite or provider HTTP directly. Its capabilities and generated command permissions are under [src-tauri/capabilities](../src-tauri/capabilities/main-window.json) and [src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated](../src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated).

## Rust state and transaction ownership

There is one mail core. `GmailCore` ([gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs)) serves two kinds of session, distinguished by an explicit `SessionPolicy` ([gmail/session.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/session.rs)): a Gmail session over the live provider, and a synthetic (fixture) session over `SyntheticGmailProvider` ([synthetic/](../crates/mail-core/src/synthetic)), whose 18 conversations and per-message INBOX/UNREAD/STARRED facts live in a transactional, seed-once `synthetic-provider.db`. The policy decides identity and status, admission, lifecycle rejections, cached-only search, local readiness and restart behaviour (interrupted unlanded writes are requeued for a synthetic session and never auto-replayed for Gmail). Command acceptance returns receipts after persistence; provider work is performed by a worker outside the acceptance transaction. Worker recovery and undo state are durable.

The Gmail session is implemented in [gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs), [gmail/store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store.rs), [gmail/operations.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs), and the Gmail provider modules. The sync service owns the Gmail cache and coordinates provider reads and queued operations. SQLite transactions persist local state; network calls occur through the provider path. [gmail/provider.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider.rs) owns HTTP, credentials, pacing, status, and quota handling; [gmail/provider/api.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider/api.rs) implements the `GmailProvider` trait (auth/session, reads and writes; defined in [gmail/types.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/types.rs)) for the concrete `LiveGmailProvider`; [gmail/parse.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/parse.rs) contains pure Gmail response and message parsing. OAuth flow, token access, and secret storage are in [gmail/auth.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs) and [gmail/secrets.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs). The service exposes account status and sync state through DTOs. Runtime success on a supported macOS installation is a separate validation question; see [current status](current-status.md).

Gmail schema upgrades are owned by `gmail/store_schema.rs`. The authoritative
`meta.schema_version` advances through `gmail-migrations-1` to
`gmail-migrations-9`, with each stage's DDL, backfills and marker in one
transaction. Pre-numbered `gmail-1` and `gmail-2` profiles had ambiguous physical
layouts, so only those historical migration bodies inspect optional columns.
An already-current profile performs no migration writes. Fresh profiles use the
canonical schema captured from the pre-change store. Unknown or newer markers
fail before schema changes. Startup crash recovery runs explicitly after
migration: globally applying operations become uncertain and lose `last_error`.
Reconnect recovery remains account-scoped and additionally clears `failure`;
these distinct semantics are preserved.

`GmailStore` stays one type owning the single SQLite connection; its impl and
helpers are split by responsibility under `gmail/store/`. `store.rs` holds the
shared types and the struct; every method that opens a transaction still opens
exactly one, so acceptance and reconciliation keep their atomic scope.

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `profile` | open and startup recovery, account identity, generation, sync checkpoints, disconnect cleanup, saved split |
| `cache`, `cache_rows` | cached conversation reads; thread and fact upserts, eviction, conversation building, `meta` helpers |
| `ingestion` | discovery and history pages, rediscovery |
| `search`, `search_support` | cached search, done, trash and starred lists; search admission and eviction |
| `acceptance`, `operation_rows` | single-operation acceptance and retry; acceptance transaction, preimages, operation row codecs |
| `worker` | claim, confirm, reconcile, defer, requeue and finish; a definitely rejected write fails on its own and the pass moves on to the next queued write, while transient and account-wide errors requeue it and back off |
| `undo`, `undo_support` | single-operation undo and its compensation helpers |
| `group_acceptance`, `group_queries`, `group_undo`, `group_rows` | group acceptance, status queries, group undo and the shared group row helpers |
| `activity` | effective conversation state and the activity list |
| `reminders`, `destinations` | local reminders; destination snapshots |

Store tests live in `gmail/store_tests.rs` beside `migration_tests.rs`.

Storage failures are diagnosable without leaking data. Every storage failure
still reaches the wire as `MailError::StorageUnavailable`, unchanged, but the
point that produced it first logs exactly one line through the `log` facade:
the call site's `file:line`, a static cause tag (`sqlite`, `lock_poisoned`,
`thread_join`, `path_unavailable`, `missing_persisted_row` and similar) and,
for SQLite errors, the primary result code name and extended code. The line
is built only from static strings and numbers; the Display text of the
underlying error is never read, because SQLite messages can quote values and
SQL. `mail-core` owns the helper in [storage_log.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/storage_log.rs);
the shell has its own small helper and the stderr logger in
[diagnostics.rs](../src-tauri/src/diagnostics.rs), which passes only the two
storage log targets and drops everything else. Re-mapping an error that was
already a `MailError` does not log a second time. Rejections because the sync
worker is stopped or halted are not logged: the failure that halted it already was.

Drafts are stored in a separate `<selected-profile>/local-drafts` SQLite database by [drafts/store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/store.rs), with revision and account identity types in [drafts/types.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/types.rs). The store uses WAL and FULL synchronous mode. Saves and deletes are revision-checked and return receipts after commit; deletion records request tombstones so a late save cannot recreate a removed draft. The frontend draft composable and editor coordinate local edits, acknowledged saves, and error recovery in [useDrafts.ts](../src/composables/useDrafts.ts), [DraftEditorCore.vue](../src/components/DraftEditorCore.vue), and [ReplyComposer.vue](../src/components/ReplyComposer.vue). Drafts remain local to the profile and do not sync to Gmail. Which account a draft belongs to, reply revalidation against the displayed conversation, and the session epoch that rejects a reply prepared across a connect or disconnect are decided by `DraftService` in [drafts/service.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/service.rs); the shell commands only delegate to it.

The native close path uses a request/acknowledgement gate in [close_gate.rs](../src-tauri/src/close_gate.rs). The shell asks the frontend to flush and close dirty draft state; the frontend acknowledges only after the latest save is committed, and cancels close when save fails. Frontend coordination lives in [App.vue](../src/App.vue) and the draft composable. The governing contract is [vertical slice 04](vertical-slice-04.md).

## Frontend coordination

[App.vue](../src/App.vue) is the composition root for navigation, focused conversation, panels, and mailbox actions. [useMailbox.ts](../src/composables/useMailbox.ts) owns account-scoped focus and mailbox query coordination and keeps the public `Mailbox` shape. It composes focused modules that receive their dependencies as arguments rather than closing over the parent: [useMailboxSelection.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxSelection.ts) owns the UX-05 selection set, range anchor and `SELECTION_MAX` bound (the parent clears it on context, account and saved-view invalidation and prunes it after each authoritative list read), [useMailboxGroups.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxGroups.ts) owns UX-05 group dispatch, the single group notice, lost-response recovery on the original request id, partial group Undo, restart notice rehydration and the Activity group history/detail reads, [useMailboxDetailCache.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxDetailCache.ts) owns the bounded neighbor-detail cache, its TTL, the single-slot prefetch and the J/K reader loading delay (its fence is an epoch the owner bumps through `invalidateDetailCache()` on every refresh, mutation start, reader close, account change and disconnect), [useMailboxAccount.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxAccount.ts) owns authoritative account/mode status and the connect, disconnect, sync, enable-actions and cancel-upgrade lifecycle (each status read is fenced by its own request token and the session; it reports an account-identity change and a confirmed disconnect to `useMailbox` through callbacks, and `useMailbox` resets list, reader, group and selection state and bumps the session generation inside them), and [mailbox-refs.ts](../src/composables/mailbox-refs.ts) and [mailbox-session.ts](../src/composables/mailbox-session.ts) hold the shared conversation-reference helpers and the session/command-fence types. Session invalidation is an explicit argument: `useMailbox` owns the session counters and hands extracted pieces a read-only `MailboxSession` (generation and detached flag) plus the shared command fence; each async path captures the generation before its first await and drops its result when it moved. Components render the inbox, reader, composer, activity, and account controls. The client subscription events are invalidation hints; the frontend reloads through client queries.

The shell passes explicit dependencies to its extracted surface state: [useGoChord.ts](../src/composables/useGoChord.ts) handles the G-chord timer, [useActionNotice.ts](../src/composables/useActionNotice.ts) derives the action notice and Undo window, [useAccountNotes.t

# ADR 0001: Start with a single-account desktop email client

**Status:** Accepted — first-build direction and scope; not authorization to connect a mailbox or send mail.

## Context

Email OS's long-term direction is a composable email client whose views, signals, commands, and workflows can be adapted by users and agents. The [PRD](../../PRD.md) describes that destination, not a suitably narrow first build.

The immediate goal is a limited replacement for Superhuman. The user has confirmed that **one account on desktop is a good starting point**. The first build should therefore replace a complete everyday activity, rather than demonstrate a platform or add another tool alongside the existing client.

[Experiment 1](../../EXPERIMENT-01.md) proposes a read-only, teachable reply queue. That remains a possible later customization study, but handing users back to another client to reply would not validate the immediate replacement goal.

At the time of this ADR, the repository contained planning and static reviews. The narrower Slice 01 fixture baseline and Slice 02 read-only Gmail path are now implemented; see the slice contracts for their boundaries and `docs/development.md` for validation status. This ADR's broader provider-backed composition, sending, Gmail archive/read-state actions, search, and saved-view scope remains future work; macOS Slice 02 runtime validation is still pending.

## Decision

Build a **keyboard-first, single-account desktop client for a complete inbox-processing session**, with one small configurable-view capability.

The initial promise is:

> I can open Email OS, process my inbox, and finish ordinary replies without switching to Superhuman.

The primary loop is:

```text
Open inbox → navigate → read conversation → reply or archive → next
```

Optimize this loop for speed, predictable interaction, and trustworthy state before adding intelligent prioritization or general extensibility.

### Initial boundaries

- One connected account, not a unified multi-account inbox.
- One desktop operating system for the first developer build. macOS is approved for the Slice 02 pilot; the broader platform/runtime gate remains pending.
- Gmail REST is approved for the narrow, read-only disposable-account Slice 02 pilot. This does not authorize write scopes or broader provider capabilities; do not build a second provider merely to demonstrate abstraction.
- No custom Android surface in this build. An existing provider client remains the mobile fallback; this sequencing does not remove Android from the product vision.
- Manual operation must work without AI or external inference.
- Initial validation is personal dogfooding, not a recruited multi-user pilot.

## First-build scope

### 1. Inbox and reading

- Inbox list and conversation reader with enough message history to reply confidently.
- Predictable keyboard navigation, focus, and shortcuts for next/previous, open/back, reply, archive, and read/unread.
- Safe message rendering. A plain-text presentation is acceptable initially; HTML fidelity is not a reason to weaken isolation or sanitization.
- Visible loading, freshness, incomplete-context, and synchronization-error states.
- An explicit fallback to the provider client for unsupported operations or message formats.

### 2. Composition and sending

- Reply, reply-all, and simple new-message composition.
- Clearly displayed recipients, distinguishing reply from reply-all; no hidden recipient expansion.
- Draft persistence across application restart, including recipient and body edits.
- Basic file attachment upload/download, with explicit size/type limitations and failures. Inline editing, attachment previews, and sophisticated formatting are deferred.
- Explicit user-initiated sending, with visible operation status and failure recovery.

Drafts may initially be application-local. The interface must make that limitation clear: cross-device/provider draft synchronization is not promised.

### 3. Mailbox actions and search

- Archive and read/unread changes reflected in provider state, so ordinary mailbox state remains consistent with other clients.
- Immediate local feedback backed by durable staging and reconciliation, not optimistic success messages that hide failures.
- Basic search sufficient to find an older conversation. Provider-backed search is acceptable; a complete local full-text index is not required.
- Search results must disclose whether they cover the provider mailbox or only cached data.

### UX-08 bounded star decision

UX-08 explicitly adds observed per-message STARRED facts and narrow Star/Unstar
setters over the immutable inventory observed at acceptance. This is a bounded
addition to the original archive/read action set, not arbitrary label authority:
INBOX and UNREAD remain independent, and the existing durable groups, preimages,
Undo and uncertain-outcome reconciliation are reused. Legacy/partial facts stay
unknown. Cached Starred includes archived/recovery mail but never promises
provider-complete coverage. No new OAuth scope is requested; actual writes still
require the verified modify grant, explicit user action and operator-approved
disposable-account validation. The legacy archive-only fixture profile does not
gain star controls. Native macOS/provider convergence remains a separate gate.
Saved splits/search are not prerequisites and are not reimplemented here.

### UX-09 bounded destination decision

UX-09 increment A explicitly permits read-only Gmail destination metadata and
bounded provider pages for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail (excluding Spam/Trash),
Spam, Trash and existing user labels. Rationale: the 100-conversation inbox cache
cannot honestly serve those destinations. Separate timestamped SQLite snapshots
must not change inbox/history checkpoints or evict durable-operation recovery.
Provider Drafts remain read-only and distinct from application-local drafts.
This does not authorize Trash/Spam writes, sending, label create/delete, arbitrary
system-label mutation, or a second provider. Label/Move remain unavailable until
a separate durable logical-intent/recovery increment satisfies the UX-09 contract.
The Gmail readonly scope suffices for increment A; all existing real-account
and native validation gates remain. No new mailbox access is authorized here.

### 4. One configurable view

Provide one additional saved queue defined by a bounded, declarative filter over sender, domain, or existing provider labels, with a stable default order. It must reuse the ordinary reader, composer, and mailbox commands.

- A small manual editor is sufficient; no natural-language authoring is required.
- Keep the full inbox accessible. Filtering must not silently archive, relabel, or hide mail from the provider inbox.
- Store the definition locally for the first build; do not imply it follows the user to mobile.
- If referenced data is not loaded, disclose the view's coverage.

This is a small test of the composable direction, not a general rules engine. Do not add new provider permissions or mutation capabilities merely to support view configuration.

### UX-10 bounded triage decision

[UX-10 A](../ux-10-bounded-triage.md) adds read-only **known cached Trash**
browsing and observed per-message TRASH/SPAM facts. This is an explicit narrow
extension of browsing, not a complete UX-09 folder catalog or broader mutation
authority. Current observed Trash/Spam excludes a conversation from local Done
even when it has old archive evidence. Legacy absence remains unknown.

Trash/recover writes and their Undo remain deferred: archive is not trash, and
the current archive/read preimages cannot restore a multi-dimension trash side
effect. The recovery destination decision is recorded in the UX-10 contract.
Mute requires actual future-message semantics, not INBOX removal; Spam/recover
needs validated provider effects. Important/Other requires independent local view
membership and explicit scope. Sender/domain rules, Block and Unsubscribe remain
deferred pending separate bounded execution/authority contracts. No send,
arbitrary URL opener, permanent deletion or empty-Trash is introduced.

## Architecture constraints

Preserve a few internal boundaries without committing to a public SDK:

1. **Mail integration and local state:** own credentials, synchronization, message identity, caching, and reconciliation outside UI components.
2. **Views:** select and order conversations from available data; they do not execute mailbox mutations.
3. **Commands and execution:** route UI actions through one typed boundary responsible for validation, durable operation state, concurrency, and recovery.
4. **Presentation:** consume those interfaces for the default inbox and the configurable view.

Use local data for responsive navigation where available. Opening a cached conversation must not require a fresh provider request to render its cached content.

Persist drafts and staged operations across restart. Cached reading and draft editing should remain usable without a connection; full offline mailbox coverage and offline search completeness are not required. Distinguish local, pending, and provider-confirmed state.

A send with an ambiguous remote outcome must enter an explicit **outcome unknown** state and be reconciled rather than blindly retried. Do not promise universal exactly-once sending or provider-side undo after delivery.

Synchronization is required while the application is running. Guaranteed synchronization, sending, or timer execution while the application is fully quit is out of scope. Hide-versus-quit behavior must be documented.

Framework, storage implementation, shell, and reuse strategy require separate technical decisions. This ADR does not select Tauri, Electron, Rust, React, or either reviewed fork.

## Safety and release gates

Narrow scope does not justify weaker mail integrity or privacy.

Before primary-mailbox dogfooding, use synthetic fixtures and a disposable account to validate:

- Authentication refresh/revocation and secure credential storage.
- Hostile-message rendering, blocked active content, and blocked automatic remote-resource loading.
- Recipient integrity for reply, reply-all, and new messages.
- Thread/context correctness and attachment handling.
- Interrupted synchronization, recovery after restart, and changes made in another client.
- Draft recovery and pending/failed mailbox mutations after connection loss.
- Concurrent send attempts and ambiguous-send recovery without blind replay.
- Search/view coverage and unsupported-message fallbacks.

Do not put mailbox content or credentials into routine diagnostic logs. Any reused code implicated by the [email](../../security/email-review.md) or [Pebble](../../security/pebble-review.md) reviews must be fixed and tested, or demonstrated to be outside reachable paths. Those static reviews are not runtime safety certifications.

## UX-12 attachment decision (bounded download-only)

The [UX-12 contract](../ux-12-safe-attachments.md) implements the existing basic
download scope, not preview. Authenticated readonly fetch, bounded cached
descriptors, cancellation and explicit inert Downloads saves are permitted.
Unsupported Office/HTML files are download-only; files never execute or load
remote resources in the app. External HTTP(S) links require explicit choice and
protocol validation; email/draft exits stay separate. No new Gmail scopes.

Attachment preview remains deferred: no macOS restricted-renderer sandbox and
compatibility spike evidence exists for this slice. A new webview alone is not
isolation. Preview requires documented enforcement of no privileged IPC and no
automatic remote-resource loading plus platform return-path testing and a new
reviewed decision. This preserves the download-only boundary rather than
silently relaxing it to claim BROWSE-14 complete.

## Explicit non-goals

- Superhuman feature parity or a polished public launch.
- Real multiple-account activation, multiple providers, or a custom mobile client.
  UX-13A permits only the synthetic in-app workspace proof described below.
- AI classification, generated replies, or agent-authored configuration.
- Public plugins, arbitrary extension code, a marketplace, or stable external APIs.
- Follow-up automation, scheduled send, sophisticated snooze, or background execution while quit.
- UX-11 permits bounded desktop-local reminders in the fixture and Gmail
  profiles. Gmail reminders live in `gmail.db`, pin baseline IDs and a reader
  snapshot, and use account-scoped receipts and revision checks. Scheduling and
  cancellation do not stage provider mailbox operations. No-reply deadlines
  require a complete fresh thread read plus local account/generation/revision
  fences; the provider can still receive a reply after that checkpoint. This
  does not claim provider-atomic absence. No calendar, cross-device or
  fully-quit execution promise is introduced. See
  [UX-11](../ux-11-local-reminders.md) for semantics and validation gates.
- Application-owned state replication across devices.
- Complete offline mailbox search, advanced rich-text editing, attachment previews, or inline attachment composition.
- Recruitment, billing, or the customization pilot described in Experiment 1.

## UX-13 bounded decision: synthetic workspaces, native/runtime deferred

The first-build single connected account boundary remains. UX-13A explicitly
permits **two browser-only synthetic account sessions** with independent browsing
and local-only draft state. This tests account+ID isolation without activating
real accounts, extending credentials, or implying remote convergence. Existing
Inbox/cached Done capabilities are reused; absent UX-06/07 search is not silently
implemented. See [the UX-13A contract](../ux-13-independent-workspaces.md).

Choose disclosed **in-app workspaces** for this proof, not native tabs. Genuine
macOS tabs require a real Tauri feasibility/lifecycle/focus validation spike;
none is claimed from browser fixtures. Native remains one window/selected core.
Same-profile competing writers continue to be deliberately rejected by OS locks.

Do not extend native account/profile/credential ownership yet: current Gmail
credentials have an account-independent Keychain key, and the shell's close gate
assumes one editor/window. Additional profile directories alone would permit
credential leakage. A backend-owned registry, credential namespace/migration,
account-bound profile leases and app-wide close coordination need a separately
approved runtime design before real activation. No unified inbox, cross-account
search, new OAuth authority or provider writes are authorized by this exception.

## Acceptance and evaluation

After the safety gates pass, dogfood the build for **five working days**.

The target is completing ordinary desktop inbox-processing sessions in Email OS. Keep the existing client available and record every fallback, including its reason and whether it blocked completion.

Evaluate:

- **Completion:** Can ordinary read/reply/archive sessions finish here? Which missing capabilities force a switch?
- **Interaction:** Does navigation remain responsive, focus predictable, and the primary loop usable without repeated mouse intervention?
- **Trust:** Do drafts survive restart, mailbox changes converge, and failures remain visible? Any silent data loss, unintended recipient, or duplicate-send defect blocks progression.
- **Composition:** Can the additional queue be changed declaratively without a new UI/core code path?

The five-day window is an evaluation period, not a build-time estimate. A high fallback rate is evidence to revise the scope, not a reason to hide unsupported cases. Prioritize the next slice from observed blockers rather than feature count or the breadth of the PRD.

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Why not first |
|---|---|
| Read-only teachable queue | Tests customization but cannot replace a complete email-processing session. |
| Reply-only workspace | A credible smaller fallback if the client scope proves too large, but leaves general inbox triage elsewhere. |
| Configurable split inbox as the main feature | Useful later; puts configuration before proving the basic read/reply/archive experience. |
| Follow-up-oriented client | Adds timers, reply detection, and execution ownership before the underlying mail loop is trustworthy. |
| Full composable-platform MVP | Too many independent risks: mail correctness, extension contracts, agent authority, automation, and multi-device state. |

## Consequences

**Benefits:** Delivers direct personal utility, validates the mail foundation against real work, and retains a modest path toward composable workflows. Avoids making AI or platform infrastructure a dependency of ordinary email use.

**Costs:** Less differentiated initially, requires consequential send/sync engineering earlier than the read-only experiment, and deliberately leaves mobile and advanced workflows in other clients. Keyboard interaction quality becomes a core acceptance criterion rather than later polish.

**Sequencing change:** This client slice takes priority over Experiment 1. The experiment remains a proposed later study of whether personalization adds value once the application can complete the work itself. The PRD remains the long-term direction; this ADR governs the narrower first build.

**Revisit when:** Dogfooding reveals a missing capability that prevents meaningful replacement, single-account desktop use is insufficient, or implementation effort warrants narrowing to the reply-only alternative. Change the ADR explicitly rather than silently expanding scope.

# Current architecture

**Scope:** This is an inventory of architecture that exists in the source tree. It describes code paths and ownership. For feature availability and validation results, see [current status](current-status.md). For the selected first-build scope, see [ADR 0001](adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md). [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) is a historical proposal; its design recommendations are not evidence of implementation.

## Runtime and boundaries

The app has a Vue/TypeScript frontend, a Tauri 2 shell, and the Rust `mail-core` crate. The Rust crate owns persistence and provider operations. The frontend talks through a `MailClient` interface. In native mode, `createTauriMailClient` maps that interface to named Tauri commands. In browser mode, `browser-fake.ts` supplies a synthetic in-memory client. The shared interface and generated wire types are in [client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/client.ts), [tauri-client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/tauri-client.ts), [browser-fake.ts](../src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts), and [generated.ts](../src/lib/ipc/generated.ts). Rust DTOs are the source for generated TypeScript; `crates/mail-core/src/bin/generate-types.rs` generates the file.

The shared Tauri entry point in [lib.rs](../src-tauri/src/lib.rs) holds the module list and the command handler list. [setup.rs](../src-tauri/src/setup.rs) selects fixture or Gmail mode on desktop, opens the corresponding Rust core (fixture mode is the Gmail core on the built-in synthetic provider, ADR 0002) and handles window and run events; [state.rs](../src-tauri/src/state.rs) holds the single `GmailCore`, the draft service, the attachment transfer registry and the close gate; the commands under [commands/](../src-tauri/src/commands) translate IPC to core calls and emit mailbox/draft/close events. Mail rules live in `mail-core`, not the shell. Desktop [main.rs](../src-tauri/src/main.rs) is a thin launcher. Android forces fixture mode and does not run the desktop close/exit gate. A pre-existing legacy fixture database is retired once by [fixture_transition.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/fixture_transition.rs), behind a startup screen (`StartupRoot.vue`, two IPC commands). Android's generated Gradle project is under `src-tauri/gen/android`; setup and build steps are in [development guide](development.md). The webview does not access SQLite or provider HTTP directly. Its capabilities and generated command permissions are under [src-tauri/capabilities](../src-tauri/capabilities/main-window.json) and [src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated](../src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated).

## Rust state and transaction ownership

There is one mail core. `GmailCore` ([gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs)) serves two kinds of session, distinguished by an explicit `SessionPolicy` ([gmail/session.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/session.rs)): a Gmail session over the live provider, and a synthetic (fixture) session over `SyntheticGmailProvider` ([synthetic/](../crates/mail-core/src/synthetic)), whose 18 conversations and per-message INBOX/UNREAD/STARRED facts live in a transactional, seed-once `synthetic-provider.db`. The policy decides identity and status, admission, lifecycle rejections, cached-only search, local readiness and restart behaviour (interrupted unlanded writes are requeued for a synthetic session and never auto-replayed for Gmail). Command acceptance returns receipts after persistence; provider work is performed by a worker outside the acceptance transaction. Worker recovery and undo state are durable.

The Gmail session is implemented in [gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs), [gmail/store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store.rs), [gmail/operations.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs), and the Gmail provider modules. The sync service owns the Gmail cache and coordinates provider reads and queued operations. SQLite transactions persist local state; network calls occur through the provider path. [gmail/provider.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider.rs) owns HTTP, credentials, pacing, status, and quota handling; [gmail/provider/api.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider/api.rs) implements the `GmailProvider` trait (auth/session, reads and writes; defined in [gmail/types.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/types.rs)) for the concrete `LiveGmailProvider`; [gmail/parse.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/parse.rs) contains pure Gmail response and message parsing. OAuth flow, token access, and secret storage are in [gmail/auth.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs) and [gmail/secrets.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs). The service exposes account status and sync state through DTOs. Runtime success on a supported macOS installation is a separate validation question; see [current status](current-status.md).

Gmail schema upgrades are owned by `gmail/store_schema.rs`. The authoritative
`meta.schema_version` advances through `gmail-migrations-1` to
`gmail-migrations-9`, with each stage's DDL, backfills and marker in one
transaction. Pre-numbered `gmail-1` and `gmail-2` profiles had ambiguous physical
layouts, so only those historical migration bodies inspect optional columns.
An already-current profile performs no migration writes. Fresh profiles use the
canonical schema captured from the pre-change store. Unknown or newer markers
fail before schema changes. Startup crash recovery runs explicitly after
migration: globally applying operations become uncertain and lose `last_error`.
Reconnect recovery remains account-scoped and additionally clears `failure`;
these distinct semantics are preserved.

`GmailStore` stays one type owning the single SQLite connection; its impl and
helpers are split by responsibility under `gmail/store/`. `store.rs` holds the
shared types and the struct; every method that opens a transaction still opens
exactly one, so acceptance and reconciliation keep their atomic scope.

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `profile` | open and startup recovery, account identity, generation, sync checkpoints, disconnect cleanup, saved split |
| `cache`, `cache_rows` | cached conversation reads; thread and fact upserts, eviction, conversation building, `meta` helpers |
| `ingestion` | discovery and history pages, rediscovery |
| `search`, `search_support` | cached search, done, trash and starred lists; search admission and eviction |
| `acceptance`, `operation_rows` | single-operation acceptance and retry; acceptance transaction, preimages, operation row codecs |
| `worker` | claim, confirm, reconcile, defer, requeue and finish; a definitely rejected write fails on its own and the pass moves on to the next queued write, while transient and account-wide errors requeue it and back off |
| `undo`, `undo_support` | single-operation undo and its compensation helpers |
| `group_acceptance`, `group_queries`, `group_undo`, `group_rows` | group acceptance, status queries, group undo and the shared group row helpers |
| `activity` | effective conversation state and the activity list |
| `reminders`, `destinations` | local reminders; destination snapshots |

Store tests live in `gmail/store_tests.rs` beside `migration_tests.rs`.

Storage failures are diagnosable without leaking data. Every storage failure
still reaches the wire as `MailError::StorageUnavailable`, unchanged, but the
point that produced it first logs exactly one line through the `log` facade:
the call site's `file:line`, a static cause tag (`sqlite`, `lock_poisoned`,

The native close path uses a request/acknowledgement gate in [close_gate.rs](../src-tauri/src/close_gate.rs). The shell asks the frontend to flush and close dirty draft state; the frontend acknowledges only after the latest save is committed, and cancels close when save fails. ## Frontend coordination

[App.vue](../src/App.vue) is the composition root for navigation, focused conversation, panels, and mailbox actions. [useMailbox.ts](../src/composables/useMailbox.ts) owns account-scoped focus and mailbox query coordination and keeps the public `Mailbox` shape. It composes focused modules that receive their dependencies as arguments rather than closing over the parent: [useMailboxSelection.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxSelection.ts) owns the UX-05 selection set, range anchor and `SELECTION_MAX` bound (the parent clears it on context, account and saved-view invalidation and prunes it after each authoritative list read), [useMailboxGroups.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxGroups.ts) owns UX-05 group dispatch, the single group notice, lost-response recovery on the original request id, partial group Undo, restart notice rehydration and the Activity group history/detail reads, [useMailboxDetailCache.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxDetailCache.ts) owns the bounded neighbor-detail cache, its TTL, the single-slot prefetch and the J/K reader loading delay (its fence is an epoch the owner bumps through `invalidateDetailCache()` on every refresh, mutation start, reader close, account change and disconnect), [useMailboxAccount.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxAccount.ts) owns authoritative account/mode status and the connect, disconnect, sync, enable-actions and cancel-upgrade lifecycle (each status read is fenced by its own request token and the session; it reports an account-identity change and a confirmed disconnect to `useMailbox` through callbacks, and `useMailbox` resets list, reader, group and selection state and bumps the session generation inside them), and [mailbox-refs.ts](../src/composables/mailbox-refs.ts) and [mailbox-session.ts](../src/composables/mailbox-session.ts) hold the shared conversation-reference helpers and the session/command-fence types. The shell passes explicit dependencies to its extracted surface state: [useGoChord.ts](../src/composables/useGoChord.ts) handles the G-chord timer, [useActionNotice.ts](../src/composables/useActionNotice.ts) derives the action notice and Undo window, [useAccountNotes.ts](../src/composables/useAccountNotes.ts) derives account and empty-line facts, [useContactContext.ts](../src/composables/useContactContext.ts) derives contact identities and pane visibility, [useSearchSurface.ts](../src/composables/useSearchSurface.ts) owns search entry, suggestions and recent queries, [useViewportContact.ts](../src/composables/useViewportContact.ts) owns the contact disclosure, the 1000px media query and the focus handoff when it is crossed, and [useAttachmentChooser.ts](../src/composables/useAttachmentChooser.ts) owns the chooser's snapshot and the origin and scroll it returns to. Anything the scenarios do not cover (read models other than Inbox and Activity, search, drafts, reminders, durability across restart) is not covered by this guarantee. Browser tests and preview use the fake client; they cannot establish native SQLite, OAuth, OS keychain, system dialogs, or WKWebView behavior. The boundary and runtime checks are recorded in [development guidance](development.md) and [current status](current-status.md).

The `mise run check` task serially runs headless core tests, the generated IPC contract check, core formatting and clippy, frontend tests, and frontend typechecking. CI installs Linux prerequisites before running this full gate. Rendered Chromium suites remain opt-in and are not part of CI.

these distinct semantics are preserved.

shared types and the struct; every method that opens a transaction still opens

| Stars | Rust represents known/unknown star facts in [stars.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/stars.rs). Cached Starred browsing and star setters exist in Gmail and synthetic sessions; the UI shows them by the explicit `capabilities.triageSurfaces` status field. Frontend action wiring is in [action-registry.ts](../src/lib/action-registry.ts). | [UX-08](ux-08-stars.md) |
| Reminders | Rust stores account-scoped local reminder records in [reminders.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/reminders.rs); reminders follow the same local rules in every mode: scheduling hides the conversation locally, the deadline returns it, and nothing is written to a provider. Frontend time handling, preferences, and the Reminders list context are in [reminder-time.ts](../src/lib/reminder-time.ts), [reminder-preferences.ts](../src/lib/reminder-preferences.ts), and [RemindersList.vue](../src/components/RemindersList.vue), [useReminders.ts](../src/composables/useReminders.ts), and [ReminderPicker.vue](../src/components/ReminderPicker.vue). | [UX-11](ux-11-local-reminders.md) |
| Attachments | Rust validates descriptors, bytes, filenames, and destination handling in [attachments.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/attachments.rs). Gmail retrieval is authenticated and read-only; fixture mode exposes a synthetic text attachment. The shell resolves the fixed OS Downloads destination in [commands/attachments.rs](../src-tauri/src/commands/attachments.rs); admission (one transfer at a time) and cancellation live in [attachments/transfers.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/attachments/transfers.rs). The UI chooses from descriptors and tracks transfer state in [useAttachmentTransfer.ts](../src/composables/useAttachmentTransfer.ts); it has no arbitrary file picker. | [UX-12](ux-12-safe-attachments.md) |

See contracts [UX-04](ux-04-trustworthy-undo.md), [UX-05](ux-05-safe-bulk-processing.md), and [UX-10](ux-10-bounded-triage.md).

## Design proposals and limits

The source tree does not make every proposal in [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) current behavior. In particular, do not infer full multi-account/provider support, provider-synced drafts, fully quit background sync, arbitrary provider search coverage, or live macOS runtime validation from the existence of interfaces or tests. [ADR 0001](adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md), the slice contracts, feature contracts, and [current status](current-status.md) define scope and validation. content.content:
### Android fixture APK

The Android target is a fixture-only Tauri app with a viewport-driven compact phone shell
(up to 719 CSS px); browser preview uses the same layout mode. It uses the same synthetic fixture core
and SQLite profile as native fixture mode (ADR 0002). Android always selects fixture mode,
even if `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail` is present. A pre-existing legacy fixture database is retired
once behind the startup screen (closing the app is the cancel path). Gmail account controls, attachment
export, and external link dispatch are unavailable on Android. The shell returns
the typed `unsupported_platform` error for attachment export and external links. The WebView
content remains padded for safe system insets; native status and navigation bars use the app
surface color and light icons. Compact layout keeps the existing capabilities and adds no mail
engine or IPC behavior. See [ADR 0003](adr/0003-mobile-layout.md) and [UX-14](ux-14-mobile-shell.md).

The current repeatable build lane targets Linux x86_64. Install JDK 17, Android
command-line tools, platform API 35, build-tools 35.0.0, and NDK 27.2.12479018.
The project Android template pins the same NDK version. The SDK root defaults to
`$HOME/Android/Sdk`; set `ANDROID_HOME`,
`ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, `NDK_HOME`, and `JAVA_HOME` when your paths differ. Install
the SDK packages and Rust targets with:

```sh
"$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager" \
  "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" "ndk;27.2.12479018"
rustup target add aarch64-linux-android x86_64-linux-android
```

Use `mise run android:doctor` to check the local prerequisites. Then build one
debug APK containing ARM64 and x86_64 native libraries:

```sh
mise run android:build
```

The Tauri CLI builds the frontend through the configured `beforeBuildCommand`.
The APK is written under
`src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/outputs/apk/universal/debug/`. For an attached
device or emulator, `mise run android:dev` runs the development app. The
generated Gradle project and wrapper are committed; local SDK paths, Gradle
caches, and build output are ignored. To regenerate the project after changing
the Tauri Android template, install the pinned SDK/NDK first and run
`pnpm tauri android init --ci --skip-targets-install`; then review the generated
diff and restore the pinned application ID, SDK, and NDK settings if the CLI
template changes them.

For the device smoke check, build the APK and install it on an attached Android
device or emulator. Use device interaction tools to launch the app and verify:

1. The fixture inbox renders and a conversation opens.
2. Mark done works. The reader moves to a neighbouring conversation (it does not
   return to the inbox); open the inbox to confirm the count dropped. Tap Undo within
   the 10-second undo window and confirm the row returns. Mark read/unread (reader button or
   row menu) and Star/Unstar (command palette) also work.
3. Gmail controls and Files and links are absent.
4. Compose a draft, wait for “Saved locally · never sent”, then close the app
   process.
5. Relaunch the app. Confirm the archived conversation remains absent and the
   draft reopens with its exact subject and body.
6. Background Email OS, open another app, resume Email OS, and confirm the
   draft editor remains intact.

Record the device/API version, APK path, persistence results, and screenshots.
These steps passed on 2026-11-14 on an Android 15 x86_64 emulator, using APK
SHA-256 `161befa9ca00e1a8dfb8bf97ff3685415ad4d55821ea0a4fcfa6d15fc5762708`.
They were re-run on 2026-11-15 with the unified-fixture CI APK
(`19ca1a225f4c9820b82d0a5d4aa0e4c8d10e8d8700582c8f6c40f1465db4197c`); results and
open findings are in [current-status.md](current-status.md). The keyboard stayed
hidden during draft entry, so IME layout remains unverified.

Legacy reset check (when changing the transition): install an APK from before ADR
0002, archive a conversation and save a draft, then run the new APK over the same
profile. `adb install -r` is refused when the two APKs are signed with different
debug keys (`INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`, as between the CI runs used on
2026-11-15). In that case tar `fixture-profile/` out with `adb exec-out run-as
dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture tar -cf - fixture-profile`, uninstall, install the
new APK without launching it, and extract the tarball back with `adb shell run-as ...
tar -xf -`. Confirm the reset screen appears before any mailbox, closing the app
there changes nothing, accepting it shows 16 Inbox rows with the draft intact, and
`fixture-profile/backups/` holds one backup while `mail.db` is gone.

If an older APK fails during startup with a profile-lock storage error, build
and install the current version. Android uses nonblocking `flock` for profile
exclusion; desktop continues to use the standard library file lock. Keep app
data when updating so the restart-persistence check remains meaningful. The
smoke does not validate Gmail, notifications, or a mobile-specific redesign.

### Local-only `mise.local.toml`

`mise.local.toml` is **gitignored and machine-local** (`/mise.local.toml` in `.gitignore`):
it holds no secrets and must never be committed. Create it in every checkout/worktree you
use, with this canonical content:

```toml
# Local-only launcher; OAuth credentials live outside this repository.
[tools]
# Hermetic Python provider for the dev:gmail shim (no system python3 needed).
uv = "0.13.7"

[env]
# Stable local code-signing identity for the tauri dev binary. Without this,
# every rebuild is ad-hoc signed and the macOS keychain "Always Allow" grant
# for the mail-core-gmail item no longer matches, re-triggering the prompt.
APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY = "email-os-dev"

[tasks."dev:gmail"]
description = "Run native Gmail mode using the private local Desktop OAuth client"
run = 'uv run --no-project "$HOME/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py"'
```

Why each piece:

- **`[tools] uv`** — pins uv (installed by `mise install`). The `dev:gmail` task runs its
  shim via `uv run --no-project`, so no system `python3` is needed, no project venv is
  created, and the stdlib-only shim runs on a uv-managed CPython. Bump the pin when you
  want a newer uv (`0.13.7` is the current latest).
- **`[tasks."dev:gmail"]`** — runs `~/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py`, which loads the
  Desktop OAuth client from `~/.config/email-os/google-desktop-client.json` (outside the
  repo), validates the expected `project_id`, exports `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail` plus the
  client env vars, and execs `mise run dev:native`. It never prints the client secret.
  Validate the config without launching the app or making any Google request:
  `mise x -- uv run --no-project "$HOME/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py" --check`
- **`[env] APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`** (macOS only) — without this, the tauri dev binary is
  ad-hoc signed and every `cargo` rebuild changes its signature; keychain "Always Allow"
  grants are tied to the code signature, so the `mail-core-gmail` keychain prompt reappears
  on every `mise run dev:gmail`. Signing the dev binary with a stable local certificate
  keeps a single grant across rebuilds.

One-time macOS keychain setup:

1. **Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → Create a Certificate**: name it
   `email-os-dev`, identity type *Self Signed Root*, certificate type **Code Signing**
   (default validity 1 year; recreate with the same name when it expires, then re-allow
   once).
2. Run `mise run dev:gmail` once and click **Always Allow** on the "email-os wants to use
   your confidential information stored in `mail-core-gmail`" prompt. The grant is pinned
   to the `email-os-dev` identity, so rebuilds no longer prompt.
3. Do **not** set the keychain item's Access Control to "Allow all applications to access
   this item" — that silences the prompt forever but lets *any* app running as you read
   the Gmail tokens silently. Keep the per-app grant.

The stored token is one keychain generic-password entry (service `mail-core-gmail`,
account `single-profile`, `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly` — local, not synced to iCloud).
To rotate/disconnect, delete it (`security delete-generic-password -s mail-core-gmail -a
single-profile`) or use the app's disconnect action; the next `mise run dev:gmail` starts
a fresh OAuth flow. Never paste credentials into the app, logs, screenshots, or reports.

## Validation gates

See [current status](current-status.md) for the maintained feature and validation
matrix. The commands below describe what each gate checks; the baseline recorded
there is evidence supplied for `main` at `f361f57c4051c0af578af43277bed8170905548a`,
not a rerun by this documentation update. That baseline reports `mise run check`
## Running the app

**Browser preview (in-memory, not durable):** `mise run dev:web`, then open the
printed localhost URL. UX-13A mounts two explicitly synthetic **in-app account
workspaces**, each with its own labelled in-memory client and the same conversation
IDs. These are not native tabs. Switch with the account buttons or the supported
Switch account command; the current local editor must save/recover successfully
before leaving. Each workspace retains navigation/Back, selection, command query,
reader state, focus and scroll. Search and saved splits are synthetic in-memory
preview capabilities; there is no real OAuth, credentials or mailbox access in
preview.
Native mode remains a single account/window and exposes no switch command. See
[UX-13A's contract and remaining gates](ux-13-independent-workspaces.md).

**Native fixture mode (default):** `mise run dev:native`. Fixture mode runs the Gmail core on
the built-in synthetic provider ([ADR 0002](adr/0002-fixture-as-synthetic-provider.md)), so the
operation ledger (acceptance, undo, groups, reminders) is the same code Gmail mode uses:

* the app reports mode `fixture`, account `fixture-account`, connected and idle, with no mutation
  grant and an explicit `capabilities.triageSurfaces`, from its first status read (bootstrap finishes
  before the window can ask); there is no OAuth, Keychain or HTTP client;
* its files live under `<app_data_dir>/fixture-profile`: `synthetic-provider.db` (durable provider
  facts, seeded once), `gmail.db` (the core's cache and operation ledger), `profile.lock`, and
  `local-drafts/` (local drafts, separate from the mailbox);
* all 18 conversations are present (the two initially archived ones are cached, not Inbox, not
  Done). Inbox mail is seeded as a realistic read/unread mix; archive, read, star, undo, groups,
  retry, saved split, search (cached only), reminders (hide locally, no provider write), the
  `fixture-text` attachment and reply headers work through the same commands as Gmail mode; cached
  Trash, provider destinations, connect, disconnect, permission upgrade and manual sync are rejected
  with the legacy fixture's error variants;
* `EMAIL_OS_FAKE_PROVIDER=paused|reject|success` (default: success) applies to synthetic writes only
  and is fixed at launch. A write interrupted by quitting (for example while paused) is requeued and
  applied at the next launch.

**One-time retirement of a legacy fixture database.** Before this change fixture mode kept its history
in `fixture-profile/mail.db`. On the first launch after upgrading, a profile that still has that file
shows a startup screen (`FixtureTransitionGate`) before the app: the old demo mailbox history (Done and
archive history, undo history, reminders, saved split) starts fresh once, local drafts are kept, and the
old database is backed up first. The backend (`mail_core::fixture_transition`, commands
`get_fixture_transition_status` and `accept_fixture_transition`) owns the state machine, persisted in
`fixture-profile/fixture-transition.json`: a consistent `VACUUM INTO backups/mail-<utc>.db` snapshot,
integrity and row-count verification, and only then removal of `mail.db` and its side files. Closing the
window instead cancels with nothing changed (you are asked again); a crash before the verified backup
leaves the old file untouched, a crash after it resumes the removal without asking; insufficient disk
space and backup failures change nothing and can be retried; it never touches `gmail-profile`,
credentials or `local-drafts`. A fresh profile, and Gmail mode, never see the screen.

**Explicit native Gmail mode:** launch with `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail`; it uses the
separate `<app_data_dir>/gmail-profile`, never the fixture database. Local drafts
are in the separate `<app_data_dir>/gmail-profile/local-drafts` profile; disconnect
retains those drafts on this device for the same account after reconnect. Set the
Google client environment before launching:

```sh
EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail \
EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID='your-desktop-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com' \
EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET='optional-desktop-client-secret' \
mise run dev:native
```

The client secret is optional. It belongs only in the local launch environment,
not source control, frontend state, logs, or a shell history copied into a report.
Initial connection requests only `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly`.
Missing/blank client ID shows `Not configured` in Gmail mode; it does not fail app
startup or fall back to the fixture. Unsupported Keychain platforms fail closed.
Mailbox controls stay disabled until the user selects **Enable mailbox actions**
and Google returns a verified modify grant for the same authenticated account.
That upgrade requests `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify`; Google's
scope is broader than this app's implemented archive/unarchive, read/unread,
and star/unstar commands and can authorize other mailbox changes (including sending or deleting
mail). The app does not provide those broader provider actions or arbitrary
labels. Its plain-text composer saves local-only drafts; sending and
provider-synced drafts are not implemented. Denial or cancellation leaves the read-only account and cached reading
available.

### Google Desktop OAuth setup (disposable account only)

For the explicitly approved Mac smoke path, use a dedicated Google Cloud project
and disposable Gmail account, not a primary/personal mailbox:

1. Enable the **Gmail API** in the project.
2. Configure the OAuth consent screen and add the disposable account as a test
   user when the app is in **Testing** status.
3. Create an OAuth client of type **Desktop app**. Put its client ID in
   `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`; the optional client secret goes only in
   `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in the launch environment.
4. Confirm initial connection requests only `gmail.readonly`. The separate
   **Enable mailbox actions** flow requests Google's broader `gmail.modify` scope
   only after explicit user opt-in; do not add any other Gmail scopes.
5. On first use, review the macOS Keychain access prompt and allow the app to use
   its Gmail credential item. Credential-storage failures are visible and fail
   closed; there is no plaintext fallback.

Google OAuth clients left in Testing can issue refresh tokens that expire after
seven days for these Gmail scopes. Plan for a fresh sign-in during testing; this
is not a reason to log or persist tokens elsewhere. A terminal-launched Tauri
process inherits that terminal's environment. Finder-launched apps generally do
not inherit the shell's exported variables; if configuration appears missing,
use the documented launch environment for the app rather than silently selecting
fixture mode. Never paste secrets into the UI or a bug report.

Disconnect removes credentials from this app's Keychain item and clears the
local Gmail profile/cache. It is a **local disconnect**, not a promise to revoke
the Google grant or revoke tokens remotely; revoke authorization through the
Google account controls separately if required.

### Gmail sync pacing and rate limits

The disposable-account diagnostic observed HTTP 403 `rateLimitExceeded` after
~60 rapid thread reads, so discovery is paced for read-only Gmail quotas:
`threads.list` discovery pages request 25 threads (the overall disclosed cap
stays 100 conversations), consecutive Gmail API reads are separated by a
100 ms minimum interval whose wait aborts promptly on cancellation, and a
mid-page failure commits the threads already fetched (the page token is not
advanced), so a rate-limit retry or restart resumes from durable progress
instead of re-fetching saved threads. HTTP 403 is classified by bounded
structured Google error reasons: only genuine quota rejections (e.g.
`rateLimitExceeded`, `userRateLimitExceeded`, `dailyLimitExceeded`,
`quotaExceeded`, `resourceExhausted`) surface as `rate_limited`; permission
denials and unclassifiable bodies surface as the generic provider error. Raw
response bodies, messages, mailbox data, or URLs with IDs are never logged or
exposed over IPC.

### Disposable Mac smoke checklist (Slice 02 prior operator validation)
## Account, connection and first run (Gmail mode)

With no usable account the Inbox says why instead of claiming it is empty: **Not
connected** with an inline **Connect Gmail**, **Sign-in expired** with **Sign in
again**, **Finish sign-in in your browser** with **Cancel sign-in**, **Syncing first
mail… N cached**, **Sync failed: …** with **Retry** (the network cause always reads
**no network**), **Initial sync has not finished** with **Sync now**, or (not
configured) a link to Account with the next step (add a Google client ID to the
launch environment, then restart). Only a connected, fully synced, empty account
shows the real empty text. In a zero-row state the sentence echoes its tone, the
same as the header note: Coral Fault for a failed sync, Amber Notice for an
expired sign-in, Ash otherwise (the words stay; the action link and hint keep their
own colours). Under **Not connected** one line says what Connect does
(it opens Google sign-in in the browser and starts read-only, so Email OS cannot
change mail until you enable mailbox actions). **In a zero-row state the empty line
owns the status sentence:** the header shows only the Preview tag, and its status
note stays only as one hidden announcement. With rows the header status note
repeats the connection or sync fact (Not connected, Sign-in expired, Syncing…,
Sync failed with its cause in words, for example Sync failed · no network; there
is no Offline wording); its action link is shown only when the empty line is not
carrying the action. While the Account drawer shows a sync failure as an alert,
the header note drops its words and link and stays silent, so the failure and its
Retry are seen and announced once (the Preview tag stays); the empty line behind
the drawer keeps its sentence but drops its own Retry until the drawer closes. Any status note replaces
the read-only hint, which at 1100px and below collapses to its Review access link.
At 1100px and below the Preview tag yields first (short `Preview`, then only its
accessible text while a note or the hint needs room); `Sync failed` and the action
link never clip, and the cause words are whole or hidden together with their
dot (never cut to a fragment); the cause stays in the note's title, the drawer and
the empty line. jsdom cannot measure layout:
the CSS is pinned by `tests/layout/account-header-css.test.ts`, and the widths at
1030px and the contact-column collapse by the opt-in rendered suite
`tests/layout/account-header.rendered.test.ts` (real Chrome, in-memory fake).
When the empty line becomes the owner of an actionable status and nothing is
focused (and no drawer, palette, reader, compose, search or contact surface is
open), focus moves once to its action; Enter or Space on the focused line runs the
same action. Focus the user already holds is never taken. The note is absent while
connected and idle. One name per action everywhere:
**Connect Gmail**, **Sign in again**, **Cancel sign-in**, **Retry**, **Sync now**.
The Account drawer shows the permission mode and the Sync section only where they
are real (not while disconnected, not configured or signing in); a signed-out
account keeps its mode and cached count but not the `Idle` or `Never synced` words.
**Connect Gmail** is offered only while disconnected and **Sign in again** after
expiry: a device that is not configured has no client ID to connect with, so there
is no Connect button, palette command or Provider mail link, only the next step.
**Connect Gmail** (or **Sign in again**) and **Sync now** are palette commands only while they can run
(Connect ranks above Go to; during a sync failure the Account group leads the
palette), and `G` then `A` (within 1 second, Gmail mode only) opens Account. The
contact column is not rendered while a ready list has no rows (no reader, no reply
target): the list takes its width and, below 1000px, the rail has no Contact button.
It returns as soon as rows exist, and stays while the list is loading or failed.
None of these gates mailbox actions: actions depend on `mutationAccess`, not on the
connection. All of it is verified with the synthetic in-memory fake; real OAuth,
sync and Keychain behavior stay operator-gated.

### Local-only `mise.local.toml`

`mise.local.toml` is **gitignored and machine-local** (`/mise.local.toml` in `.gitignore`):
it holds no secrets and must never be committed. Create it in every checkout/worktree you
use, with this canonical content:

```toml
# Local-only launcher; OAuth credentials live outside this repository.
[tools]
# Hermetic Python provider for the dev:gmail shim (no system python3 needed).
uv = "0.13.7"

[env]
# Stable local code-signing identity for the tauri dev binary. Without this,
# every rebuild is ad-hoc signed and the macOS keychain "Always Allow" grant
# for the mail-core-gmail item no longer matches, re-triggering the prompt.
APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY = "email-os-dev"

[tasks."dev:gmail"]
description = "Run native Gmail mode using the private local Desktop OAuth client"
run = 'uv run --no-project "$HOME/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py"'
```

Why each piece:

- **`[tools] uv`** — pins uv (installed by `mise install`). The `dev:gmail` task runs its
  shim via `uv run --no-project`, so no system `python3` is needed, no project venv is
  created, and the stdlib-only shim runs on a uv-managed CPython. Bump the pin when you
  want a newer uv (`0.13.7` is the current latest).
- **`[tasks."dev:gmail"]`** — runs `~/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py`, which loads the
  Desktop OAuth client from `~/.config/email-os/google-desktop-client.json` (outside the
  repo), validates the expected `project_id`, exports `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail` plus the
  client env vars, and execs `mise run dev:native`. It never prints the client secret.
  Validate the config without launching the app or making any Google request:
  `mise x -- uv run --no-project "$HOME/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py" --check`
- **`[env] APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`** (macOS only) — without this, the tauri dev binary is
  ad-hoc signed and every `cargo` rebuild changes its signature; keychain "Always Allow"
  grants are tied to the code signature, so the `mail-core-gmail` keychain prompt reappears
  on every `mise run dev:gmail`. Signing the dev binary with a stable local certificate
  keeps a single grant across rebuilds.

One-time macOS keychain setup:

1. **Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → Create a Certificate**: name it
   `email-os-dev`, identity type *Self Signed Root*, certificate type **Code Signing**
   (default validity 1 year; recreate with the same name when it expires, then re-allow
   once).
2. Run `mise run dev:gmail` once and click **Always Allow** on the "email-os wants to use
   your confidential information stored in `mail-core-gmail`" prompt. The grant is pinned
   to the `email-os-dev` identity, so rebuilds no longer prompt.
3. Do **not** set the keychain item's Access Control to "Allow all applications to access
   this item" — that silences the prompt forever but lets *any* app running as you read
   the Gmail tokens silently. Keep the per-app grant.

The stored token is one keychain generic-password entry (service `mail-core-gmail`,
account `single-profile`, `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly` — local, not synced to iCloud).
To rotate/disconnect, delete it (`security delete-generic-password -s mail-core-gmail -a
single-profile`) or use the app's disconnect action; the next `mise run dev:gmail` starts
a fresh OAuth flow. Never paste credentials into the app, logs, screenshots, or reports.

## Running the app

**Browser preview (in-memory, not durable):** `mise run dev:web`, then open the
printed localhost URL. UX-13A mounts two explicitly synthetic **in-app account
workspaces**, each with its own labelled in-memory client and the same conversation
IDs. These are not native tabs. Switch with the account buttons or the supported
Switch account command; the current local editor must save/recover successfully
before leaving. Each workspace retains navigation/Back, selection, command query,
reader state, focus and scroll. Search and saved splits are synthetic in-memory
preview capabilities; there is no real OAuth, credentials or mailbox access in
preview.
Native mode remains a single account/window and exposes no switch command. See
[UX-13A's contract and remaining gates](ux-13-independent-workspaces.md).

**Native fixture mode (default):** `mise run dev:native`. Fixture mode runs the Gmail core on
the built-in synthetic provider ([ADR 0002](adr/0002-fixture-as-synthetic-provider.md)), so the
operation ledger (acceptance, undo, groups, reminders) is the same code Gmail mode uses:

* the app reports mode `fixture`, account `fixture-account`, connected and idle, with no mutation
  grant and an explicit `capabilities.triageSurfaces`, from its first status read (bootstrap finishes
  before the window can ask); there is no OAuth, Keychain or HTTP client;
* its files live under `<app_data_dir>/fixture-profile`: `synthetic-provider.db` (durable provider
  facts, seeded once), `gmail.db` (the core's cache and operation ledger), `profile.lock`, and
  `local-drafts/` (local drafts, separate from the mailbox);
* all 18 conversations are present (the two initially archived ones are cached, not Inbox, not
  Done). Inbox mail is seeded as a realistic read/unread mix; archive, read, star, undo, groups,
  retry, saved split, search (cached only), reminders (hide locally, no provider write), the
  `fixture-text` attachment and reply headers work through the same commands as Gmail mode; cached
  Trash, provider destinations, connect, disconnect, permission upgrade and manual sync are rejected
  with the legacy fixture's error variants;
* `EMAIL_OS_FAKE_PROVIDER=paused|reject|success` (default: success) applies to synthetic writes only
  and is fixed at launch. A write interrupted by quitting (for example while paused) is requeued and
  applied at the next launch.

**One-time retirement of a legacy fixture database.** Before this change fixture mode kept its history
in `fixture-profile/mail.db`. On the first launch after upgrading, a profile that still has that file
shows a startup screen (`FixtureTransitionGate`) before the app: the old demo mailbox history (Done and
archive history, undo history, reminders, saved split) starts fresh once, local drafts are kept, and the
old database is backed up first. The backend (`mail_core::fixture_transition`, commands
`get_fixture_transition_status` and `accept_fixture_transition`) owns the state machine, persisted in
`fixture-profile/fixture-transition.json`: a consistent `VACUUM INTO backups/mail-<utc>.db` snapshot,
integrity and row-count verification, and only then removal of `mail.db` and its side files. Closing the
window instead cancels with nothing changed (you are asked again); a crash before the verified backup
leaves the old file untouched, a crash after it resumes the removal without asking; insufficient disk
space and backup failures change nothing and can be retried; it never touches `gmail-profile`,
credentials or `local-drafts`. A fresh profile, and Gmail mode, never see the screen.

**Explicit native Gmail mode:** launch with `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail`; it uses the
separate `<app_data_dir>/gmail-profile`, never the fixture database. Local drafts
are in the separate `<app_data_dir>/gmail-profile/local-drafts` profile; disconnect
retains those drafts on this device for the same account after reconnect. Set the
Google client environment before launching:

```sh
EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail \
EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID='your-desktop-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com' \
EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET='optional-desktop-client-secret' \
mise run dev:native
```

The client secret is optional. It belongs only in the local launch environment,
not source control, frontend state, logs, or a shell history copied into a report.
Initial connection requests only `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly`.
Missing/blank client ID shows `Not configured` in Gmail mode; it does not fail app
startup or fall back to the fixture. Unsupported Keychain platforms fail closed.
Mailbox controls stay disabled until the user selects **Enable mailbox actions**
and Google returns a verified modify grant for the same authenticated account.
That upgrade requests `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify`; Google's
scope is broader than this app's implemented archive/unarchive, read/unread,
and star/unstar commands and can authorize other mailbox changes (including sending or deleting
mail). The app does not provide those broader provider actions or arbitrary
labels. Its plain-text composer saves local-only drafts; sending and
provider-synced drafts are not implemented. Denial or cancellation leaves the read-only account and cached reading
available.

### Google Desktop OAuth setup (disposable account only)

For the explicitly approved Mac smoke path, use a dedicated Google Cloud project
and disposable Gmail account, not a primary/personal mailbox:

1. Enable the **Gmail API** in the project.
2. Configure the OAuth consent screen and add the disposable account as a test
   user when the app is in **Testing** status.
3. Create an OAuth client of type **Desktop app**. Put its client ID in
   `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`; the optional client secret goes only in
   `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in the launch environment.
4. Confirm initial connection requests only `gmail.readonly`. The separate
   **Enable mailbox actions** flow requests Google's broader `gmail.modify` scope
   only after explicit user opt-in; do not add any other Gmail scopes.
5. On first use, review the macOS Keychain access prompt and allow the app to use
   its Gmail credential item. Credential-storage failures are visible and fail
   closed; there is no plaintext fallback.

Google OAuth clients left in Testing can issue refresh tokens that expire after
seven days for these Gmail scopes. Plan for a fresh sign-in during testing; this
is not a reason to log or persist tokens elsewhere. A terminal-launched Tauri
process inherits that terminal's environment. Finder-launched apps generally do
not inherit the shell's exported variables; if configuration appears missing,
use the documented launch environment for the app rather than silently selecting
fixture mode. Never paste secrets into the UI or a bug report.

Disconnect removes credentials from this app's Keychain item and clears the
local Gmail profile/cache. It is a **local disconnect**, not a promise to revoke
the Google grant or revoke tokens remotely; revoke authorization through the
Google account controls separately if required.

### Gmail sync pacing and rate limits

The disposable-account diagnostic observed HTTP 403 `rateLimitExceeded` after
~60 rapid thread reads, so discovery is paced for read-only Gmail quotas:
`threads.list` discovery pages request 25 threads (the overall disclosed cap
stays 100 conversations), consecutive Gmail API reads are separated by a
100 ms minimum interval whose wait aborts promptly on cancellation, and a
mid-page failure commits the threads already fetched (the page token is not
advanced), so a rate-limit retry or restart resumes from durable progress
instead of re-fetching saved threads. HTTP 403 is classified by bounded
structured Google error reasons: only genuine quota rejections (e.g.
`rateLimitExceeded`, `userRateLimitExceeded`, `dailyLimitExceeded`,
`quotaExceeded`, `resourceExhausted`) surface as `rate_limited`; permission
denials and unclassifiable bodies surface as the generic provider error. Raw
response bodies, messages, mailbox data, or URLs with IDs are never logged or
exposed over IPC.
